ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Settlement Hearing Comes into Focus [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: A hearing on the Anthropic copyright settlement is taking shape, with details emerging about the process and scope of the case. The story follows earlier reports that thousands of authors are seeking a share of the settlement, making it one of the most significant AI copyright cases in publishing.

ip_top_stories.title: Thousands of authors seek share of Anthropic copyright settlement
ip_top_stories.summary: Large numbers of authors are registering claims in the Anthropic copyright settlement, underscoring the breadth of the case and the scale of creator interest in compensation for alleged unauthorised training data use. The case is being closely watched as a potential bellwether for AI and copyright liability.

ip_top_stories.title: Recent Decisions Reshape Copyright Liability for AI Platforms and Their Users
ip_top_stories.summary: A review of recent court decisions examines how emerging rulings are redefining copyright liability for AI platforms and the users who deploy them. The analysis covers key judgments that are shifting the legal landscape for both AI developers and content creators.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: A comprehensive review of EU copyright law developments in the first quarter of 2026, covering legislative updates and key decisions relevant to AI and intellectual property. The roundup provides an authoritative overview of how European copyright frameworks are evolving in response to AI.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Music Generator Can't Duck DMCA Claim
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has ruled that a DMCA copyright claim against an AI music generator can proceed, in a decision with significant implications for AI-generated content and platform liability. The ruling adds to a growing body of case law testing the boundaries of copyright protection in AI contexts.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the shifting legal and commercial trends emerging from disputes between copyright holders and AI developers, tracking how the landscape is evolving globally.

ip_further_links.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_further_links.summary: The famous monkey selfie copyright case is being cited as an inadvertent precedent in emerging AI copyright disputes over authorship and ownership of machine-generated works.

ip_further_links.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of whether the UK government's approach to AI copyright exceptions is hampering domestic AI development while failing to adequately protect rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: As publishers block the Wayback Machine over AI scraping fears, the preservation of the web's public record is threatened
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers increasingly blocking the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine to prevent AI scraping is raising concerns about the long-term preservation of the public web record.

ip_further_links.title: Australian Creatives Push Back Against 'AI Theft'
ip_further_links.summary: Australian artists and creators are mounting organised opposition to AI companies using their work without consent or compensation, calling for stronger legal protections.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or regulatory committee has recommended mandatory labelling of AI-generated content to enable the public to identify synthetic media more easily.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: China has introduced tightened examination standards for AI-related patent applications, with analysis exploring what the new rules mean for AI innovators seeking IP protection.

ip_further_links.title: At Conference on the Copyright Act's 50th Anniversary, Professor Paul Goldstein Looks to the AI Era
ip_further_links.summary: Leading copyright scholar Professor Paul Goldstein addressed the Copyright Act's 50th anniversary conference, reflecting on how the existing legal framework may need to adapt to the challenges posed by AI.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A look at the specialist copyright lawyers increasingly being retained by AI startups to navigate growing legal exposure over training data, licensing, and infringement claims.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: An exploration of the unresolved legal question of who holds copyright in AI-generated artworks, examining current legal positions across jurisdictions and potential legislative responses.
